Pollock received solid support from opener Doug Watson, who
chiselled 75 runs after six and a half hours at the crease,
after the Natal top order had once again been shaken up by the
intelligent pace bowling of the 26-year-old Vasbert Drakes.
Getting the ball to swing away from the right-handed
batsmen, the West Indian took three wickets for just seven runs

But captain Dale Benkenstein, century-maker in the first
innings, initiated the recovery as he and Watson added 56 for
the fourth-wicket. The 22-year-old struck eight elegant fours
through the covers during a fluent 41 before being given out leg
befor wicket to the medium pace of Piet Botha.
Watson was then joined by Pollock and the pair put on 113
for the sixth wicket either side of lunch with Pollock going on
to record his highest score in the competition.
Having been at the crease for three hours, faced 106 balls
and struck nine fours and a six, Pollock drove Botha uppishly to
Watson, who had earlier posted the third-slowest first-class
50 at Kingsmead in 283 minutes, departed after hooking the
medium pace of Brendan Horan to Vasbert Drakes at fine leg.
